mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 for 3 consecutive months indicates strong supply-side expansion, which typically supports corporate profit growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during late-cycle expansion regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO exceeds 105.0 for 3 consecutive months during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals rising inflation expectations, which typically leads to a repricing of equity valuations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the Federal Reserve may accelerate tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% for a single month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 1.5%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 104.0 indicates a weakening economy, which typically leads to a reversal in the tightening cycle and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Fed may pivot to easing.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5% and INDPRO falls below 104.0, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 per month indicates robust labor market growth, which typically supports consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 104.0 signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates a weakening economy and potential recession.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls below 104.0 for a single month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
